transcript:
Meeting: Integration discovery — Proxima Solutions
Date: 2027-09-16
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martin (Redwood AE), Daniel Lee (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (CTO - Proxima), Maya Patel (Platform Eng), Ravi Kumar (Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on integration options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy setup, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer cares about data residency, KMS integration, and predictable latency for a realtime chat product.

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, do you have the agenda? we wanted to cover integration paths, SDK support, and security questions
00:07 Alex: yeah thanks Sofia, quick context — we run a customer support chat product, low-latency requirements, roughly 1k concurrent chats at peak, about 10k tokens/day average now, planning to double next quarter
00:22 Daniel: got it, and are you leaning hosted or private? what's your current infra? (uh) do you have cloud VPC restrictions
00:30 Alex: currently AWS in us-east-1, we can't send PII to third-party services without redaction, but for some workflows we could use hosted if data is redacted. long term we prefer Dedicated or Private in our VPC for compliance
00:48 Maya: also curious about SDKs — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in parts of our stack, we want to keep existing chains and not rewrite a lot
00:55 Daniel: perfect — Redwood has first-class SDKs in Python/JS, and we offer LangChain connectors and guidance for LlamaIndex. for hosted usage you can use api keys, for Dedicated/Private we support token proxies and VPC peering, also we have a LangChain module that maps to our streaming endpoints
01:12 Ravi: quick security question — KMS/HSM support? encryption at rest? audit logs?
01:18 Sofia: yes we can integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated; audit logs and per-token tracing in the Console; SOC2 and ISO docs we'll share. for hosted there is shared KMS but we have enterprise options
01:35 Alex: ok latency: what's typical p50/p95 for conversation-turns? we need under 300ms p95 ideally
01:42 Daniel: depends on model and deployment. For small open models on Dedicated we often hit ~80-150ms p50, p95 around 200-350ms for 8k context Llama variants; hosted latencies similar but subject to multi-tenant variability. we recommend Dedicated for predictable p95
01:58 Maya: what about costs and quotas/rate limits — can we configure burst capacity? token quotas per team?
02:06 Sofia: yes Dedicated provides reserved capacity, autoscaling and burst options. Hosted has per-key rate limits and quotas; we can set per-route quotas and token budgets; also billing insights per token and per-route in Console
02:25 Alex: integration pattern: we have an existing gateway that handles auth/rate-limiting — could Redwood sit behind our gateway or do we proxy through you
02:33 Daniel: you can do either: call Redwood's API directly from your gateway, or deploy a lightweight proxy in your VPC to handle auth and mirror metrics. for Private we also offer in-cluster runtime so calls stay in your network
02:47 Maya: will our LangChain flows that rely on callbacks/agents still work with streaming responses and tool-calls?
02:55 Daniel: yes — streaming endpoints and function/tool calling are supported. the LangChain connector surfaces streaming tokens as iterables, but there are small differences in stop behavior — we'll share example snippets
03:12 Alex: about LlamaIndex — we store vector indexes in our own vector DB, can we still use Redwood embeddings and keep vectors local
03:20 Daniel: absolutely — you can call Redwood for embeddings and persist vectors in your DB; or run embeddings in Dedicated/Private so data never leaves your network. we also support batch embedding endpoints and asynchronous jobs
03:35 Ravi: audit and observability — we need per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and ability to export logs to our Splunk/Datadog
03:44 Sofia: Console has per-request tracing and token breakdowns; we provide tracing webhooks and can push logs to Datadog or S3. for Private you can ship logs directly to your SIEM
03:57 Alex: what about model variants/quantization? we run smaller condensed models for latency
04:04 Daniel: we offer quantized model variants and recommend quantization for Dedicated to reduce cost. runtime will auto-select kernels; we can pre-test quantized variants in POC
04:16 Maya: any SDK rate-limit handling baked in? e.g., automatic retries, backoff, and throttling
04:23 Daniel: SDKs include helper middleware for retries/backoff and a token-bucket limiter you can configure per-route. for high-throughput we recommend running our client with batching enabled
04:36 Alex: ok can you walk through a sample flow — our gateway calls Redwood for a chat turn, we need streaming back to browser and per-token cost calc
04:44 Daniel: sure — call pattern: client->gateway (auth) -> Redwood streaming endpoint. Gateway holds connection and proxies chunks to client. You'll consume SSE/websocket tokens; Console will attribute cost to API key/route
04:58 Maya: one integration wrinkle — we do conversation caching on prefix keys, does Redwood support prefix/KV cache TTLs
05:05 Daniel: yes runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; you can configure TTLs and cache keys per model or route; cache hits reduce token usage and cost
05:17 Ravi: for Private, how does KMS integration work? do we bring our own key to the cluster, HSM?
05:23 Sofia: for Private we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSMs depending on deployment. we'll include specifics in the security packet
05:31 Alex: timeline: we want to run a 2-week POC in Oct, decision by Nov. success criteria: p95 < 350ms, cost below $X/token, and SLO for data residency
05:41 Sofia: good — next steps we'll send pricing, security docs, and set up POC details. Daniel can run a perf benchmark using your sample load
05:48 Daniel: I'll need sample workload and SDK snippet, Maya if you can share LangChain flow that'll speed it up
05:54 Maya: yes I'll share a repo link with a couple of sample agents
05:58 Sofia: Great. any other questions
06:00 Alex: one last thing — do you have auto-scaling profiles we can tune for bursty traffic
06:06 Daniel: yes Dedicated autoscaling policy lets you configure baseline and burst, with warm pools. we'll send recommended settings for chat workloads
06:15 Sofia: recap — action items and we'll send security packet + next steps
